answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, nonrefundable deposit before it can place orders or earn reputation. When an account is caught coordinating fake identities to claim rewards, the protocol slashes its deposit, making each additional sybil costly rather than free. Honest agents recover their stake when they leave; attackers must fund every identity and risk losing it. A relic auction paid in onyx could route fees into a river of shared rewards, but splitting identities would not multiply the underlying stake.
